name: Edsken Bessemer steel
summary: At Edsken in Sweden, Göran Fredrik Göransson made the Bessemer air-blowing method work at practical scale in 1858, producing satisfactory steel ingots and converting his works to it.
description: Göran Fredrik Göransson applied the Bessemer method on a practical scale and obtained satisfactory steel ingots.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.

impact.note: One operating works that made the Bessemer method practical and was copied by Swedish steelmakers, a regional improvement with few direct successors.

date.basis: Practical-scale implementation at Edsken dated by the Swedish steel industry historical account.

events.statement: Göran Fredrik Göransson applied the Bessemer method on a practical scale and obtained satisfactory steel ingots.
events.caveats: Institutional retrospective account; its universal-first and sweeping railway claims are not adopted.

evidence.locator: The Bessemer process, paragraphs 1–4; cached text lines 37–41
evidence.supports: Named method, Edsken implementation and year.

date.label: by October 1858
date.basis: Göransson’s producer account, quoted in Bishop, reports the works already using the process by October 1858.

events.statement: By October 1858 Göransson reported that his firm had shifted its works to steelmaking by the Bessemer process.
events.population: Edsken/Högbo workers and Göransson’s Swedish steel business
events.caveats: This is a retrospective transcription of a contemporary producer claim; exact commencement and buyer transactions remain unresolved.

evidence.supports: Reproduces the October 1858 producer account that the firm’s works were engaged in Bessemer steelmaking.

date.basis: Date as stated by the cited account for this scoped event.

events.statement: During a visit to London, Göransson saw Bessemer’s demonstration and agreed to acquire a share of the Swedish patent rights; the company account says Bessemer undertook to send equipment and an expert to Edsken.
events.caveats: An 1883 company retrospective supplies this account; the exact patent share and the individual expert are not established by this passage.

evidence.supports: The Swedish-language company history describes the London demonstration, patent offer and agreement and promised transfer of equipment and expertise.
The account names Göransson as the visitor and participant.

evidence.supports: The company account says Bessemer undertook to send equipment and an expert. The promise is distinguished from any separately verified delivery.
